A la recherche du Diamant de l'Ange vert

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1225 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Poteaux-carres

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Après le carton de son livre Foot Sentimental paru il y a 3 ans aux éditions Le Cherche midi, Dominique Rocheteau a fait paraître le mois dernier dans la même maison Soif d'Idéal.
  • "C'est seulement le lendemain de notre victoire contre Kiev, puis dans les jours qui ont suivi, que j'ai commencé à prendre la mesure de ce qui venait de se passer.
  • Industry observers note that J'ai vraiment pris conscience que quelque chose avait changé lors de nos déplacements en championnat après Kiev.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Après le carton de son livre Foot Sentimental paru il y a 3 ans aux éditions Le Cherche midi, Dominique Rocheteau a fait paraître le mois dernier dans la même maison Soif d'Idéal. L'Ange Vert revient dans ce bouquin - anecdotes à l'appui - sur la Rocheteaumania qui a envahi la France après le mythique quart de finale retour de Coupe d'Europe des Clubs Champions qui s'est déroulé le 17 mars 1976 dans le Chaudron. Extraits.

"C'est seulement le lendemain de notre victoire contre Kiev, puis dans les jours qui ont suivi, que j'ai commencé à prendre la mesure de ce qui venait de se passer. Peu à peu, j'ai perçu l'ampleur de cette vague verte qui n'allait cesser de grandir, et de ce que ce match allait changer dans ma vie. À l'entraînement, une foule que je n'avais encore jamais vue pour un simple décrassage nous attendait : à l'entrée, à la sortie, tout autour du terrain. Que du vert. Cette fois, j'ai pu saluer mes parents à la sortie du stade, juste avant qu'ils ne reprennent la route. J’étais heureux, bien sûr, mais je l'avoue un peu perdu, déconcerté, face à cet engouement auquel je n'étais absolument pas préparé.

Industry observers note that J'ai vraiment pris conscience que quelque chose avait changé lors de nos déplacements en championnat après Kiev. C'était comme si toute la France était derrière nous. Et puis, il y avait les médias, plus seulement sportifs : Paris Match, Télé 7 Jours, Rock & Folk, Rolling Stones, Salut les copains, Pif Gadget… Je ne lisais pas les journaux, je ne regardais pas la télévision. J'étais un peu dans mon monde, mais désormais je devais « apprendre » à me raconter. J'acceptais les demandes, plus par politesse que par réelle envie. Je me retrouvais souvent pris de court, parfois même paniqué. Je n'avais pas d'agent. Les journalistes passaient par le club pour leurs demandes d'interview, et je me sentais obligé d'accepter. À 20 ans, je ne contrôlais rien. Un jour, je me suis rendu compte que j'avais donné une interview pour un magazine érotique… quand ils m'ont envoyé le numéro. C'est aussi après Kiev que l'on a commencé à m'appeler l’« Ange vert », un surnom que j'ai mis du temps à apprécier.

Ce qui m'a le plus désarçonné, ce sont ces sacs de courriers qui ont commencé à arriver. Que faire de tout ça ? Je lisais quelques lettres, mais il y en avait des milliers. Il y avait de tout : des demandes en mariage, des déclarations d'amour, des confidences, des photos, des messages, comme si nous nous connaissions depuis toujours. Après les vacances d'été et celles de Noël, quand je revenais de Charente-Maritime, le secrétaire de l'AS Saint-Étienne m'invitait à passer récupérer au stade des sacs postaux. « Il y en a plusieurs kilos ». Je devinais à son ton que cela représentait une charge de travail. Ils étaient remplis de lettres et parfois de cassettes audio de filles envoyant des compliments ou des messages, par exemple : « Dominique, j'aimerais bien que l'on se voit ». Certaines glissaient même un chewing-gum à l'intérieur. Beaucoup de lettres venaient de filles. Certaines m'avouaient qu'elles m'aimaient.

It has been revealed that il y avait aussi des plaisanteries comme cette lettre émanant de lycéennes d'un établissement religieux en région parisienne qui suggérait mon mariage avec une fille « de bonne famille » de leur entourage. D'autres donnaient des recettes miracles pour faire cesser les rhumes ou bien améliorer le tonus. Des collégiens racontaient aussi le plaisir qu'ils avaient à chanter pendant leurs cours la chanson « Allez les Verts » pour embêter leurs professeurs. Beaucoup de lettres venaient d'Afrique, où Saint-Étienne était très aimé. Certaines étaient longues, parfois plusieurs pages et vraiment très belles. Mais aussi des pays de l'Est -Pologne, Allemagne de l'Est, Tchécoslovaquie - d'où de nombreux collectionneurs m'envoyaient des photos parues dans les magazines afin que je les signe. J'en reçois encore aujourd'hui au siège du club qui me les fait suivre à chaque fois.

Industry observers note that mes amis Hugues et Louis - qui habitait à Saint-Héand et préparait son concours du barreau - et moi, nous nous asseyions par terre dans la salle à manger pour trier le courrier. Impossible de répondre à tout le monde. Nous envoyions une photo dédicacée à ceux qui avaient joint une enveloppe timbrée à leur nom. Certains glissaient même un billet de 20 ou 50 francs pour recevoir une photo signée. Nous remettions ensuite les enveloppes à la postière de Saint-Héand qui nous félicitait : « Joli travail ! », avant de les oblitérer. À travers toutes ces petites histoires, j'étais à la fois touché mais aussi terriblement gêné. Tout cela me paraissait énorme, démesuré. Dans la rue, j'appréciais les marques de sympathie même si elles me mettaient mal à l'aise. Je ne savais pas toujours quoi dire, alors je répondais par un sourire.

Sources indicate that un matin de juillet 1976, j'étais en vacances chez mes parents. Je dormais encore tandis que ma mère et Louis prenaient le café dans le jardin. Un jeune homme s'est présenté derrière le grillage et a demandé à me voir. Ma mère lui a demandé s'il me connaissait. Devant sa réponse affirmative et son insistance, elle a fini par le laisser entrer. Ils sont venus me réveiller. « Il y a un ami qui veut te voir ». Je me suis levé, surpris. « Je ne vous connais pas » -  « Si, je vous ai vu à un match »… « Qu'est-ce que vous voulez ? » « Un autographe ». Je me suis exécuté et il est reparti ravi. Je suis resté partagé entre la satisfaction de faire plaisir et le malaise de voir ma vie privée ainsi envahie.

In a recent development, une autre fois, peu après avoir fait construire mon chalet à La Gimont, je suis rentré de l'entraînement et j'ai constaté que mon chat, Diamant, avait disparu. Une femme était venue chez moi, l'avait emmenée et avait fait savoir à mon entourage que si je voulais le récupérer, je devais me rendre personnellement chez elle à Veauche, à une dizaine de kilomètres. Mon ami Louis a tenté de la raisonner, en vain. Que faire ? Il n'était pas question pour moi de céder à ce chantage. Je ne voulais pas y aller, mais je tenais à récupérer mon chat. Yves, le frère de Louis, a alors appelé la gendarmerie de Saint-Galmier. Les gendarmes se sont rendus à Veauche et ont réussi à convaincre la dame de rendre Diamant. Ils n'ont toutefois pas pu le ramener eux-mêmes. Sur leur conseil, Louis a sauté dans sa voiture pour aller le chercher. Quand il est arrivé, le chat était couché sur un coussin, sur une chaise. La femme lui a lancé : « Voyez, il avait déjà pris ses marques. » Grâce à Louis et à l'intervention des gendarmes, j'ai pu récupérer Diamant et une fois de plus mesurer la chance que j'avais d'avoir des amis en or. 1976 a été une année folle. Depuis Kiev, tout avait changé autour de moi, mais je n'ai jamais vraiment cherché à me protéger ni à mettre de la distance entre moi et les autres. Je voulais simplement vivre une vie normale, comme les autres jeunes de mon époque.".

In a recent development, di questa Lazio l’aspetto che mi ha impressionato, e che mi dà sicurezza per il futuro, è che non hanno staccato la spina. Questo non è importante, di più. Significa che chi era a Roma durante la sosta ha voluto dimostrare di stare sul pezzo, di meritare spazio”.

In a recent development, hugo Cuypers, le Belge le plus prolifique ces derniers mois, peut espérer monter en grade après avoir fêté sa première sélection. Chivu vede in lui la soluzione perfetta per un reparto che necessita di interventi mirati in ottica presente e futura.

Tuttavia, l'operazione si prospetta complessa: Claudio Lotito non ha intenzione di svendere il danese  e per privarsi del difensore a gennaio chiederebbe una cifra vicina ai 40 milioni di euro. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

Industry observers note that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct problems with City that Maresca must fix. A newly introduced midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

Sources indicate that A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

In a recent development, his team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Industry observers note that maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Recent findings suggest that momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he mentioned. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

His team indicated an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, latest signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

According to recent reports, they could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

It has been revealed that brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. In a recent development, pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he remarked of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s significant idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

In a recent development, the Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

It has been revealed that welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a fresh era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut….

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, S'il n'a pas encore joué de match officiel en équipe première sous le maillot vert depuis son arrivée dans le Forez le 2 février dernier, Marten-Chris Paalberg, actuellement sous contrat avec l'ASSE jusqu'en 2030, a démarré cet automne 3 matches avec la réserve : 1 en Challenge Espoirs (0-2 face au Mans) et 2 en National 2 (1-1 à Montpellier). Venant d'enchaîner 2 succès en équipe d'Estonie (le premier en sortie de banc au Luxembourg et le second en tant que titulaire contre la Bulgarie), le prometteur attaquant de 18 ans s'est longuement confié à Soccernet. Un long et intéressant entretien que nous avons traduit pour vous !

"Je suis maintenant en pleine forme ! Nouveau club, nouvel environnement. Je pense avoir progressé et maintenant, je vais pouvoir le montrer. Ma santé actuellement ? Disons que tout va bien. Comme j'ai eu des problèmes au genou pendant très longtemps, il arrive que, lorsque les entraînements ou les matchs sont particulièrement intenses, je ressente quelques sensations différentes le lendemain. Mais pour le moment, tout va bien. J'enchaîne les matchs, j'accumule du temps de jeu et je n'ai aucune raison de me plaindre.

Pour être honnête, je ne sais pas exactement quel était mon problème au genou. Tout ce que je peux dire, c'est qu'il y avait un problème au niveau de la rotule et du tendon. À la fin, c'est devenu chronique, ce qui explique pourquoi cela a pris autant de temps. Mais je ne connais pas exactement le diagnostic de mémoire. Je n'ai aucune restriction, mais au sein de l'équipe, on souhaite que je prenne un jour de repos supplémentaire en milieu de semaine après les journées les plus intenses. Ce n'est pas vraiment une restriction, puisque c'est aussi une journée de récupération pour le reste de l'équipe. De mon côté, je fais simplement quelques exercices avec les kinés à l'intérieur.

Mon adaptation et ma vie en France ? J'ai maintenant pris mes marques. Je suis également devenu plus proche de mes coéquipiers et nous sortons régulièrement ensemble. L'année dernière, c'était un peu plus compliqué, mais maintenant tout est facile et tout va bien. Je m'entraîne tous les jours avec les professionnels. Pour le moment, je joue simplement avec la réserve. Mais mon environnement de travail quotidien reste bien celui de l'équipe première.

Je ne peux pas dire quand je ferai mes débuts en équipe première, c'est à l'entraîneur de décider. Pour le moment, la situation est compliquée : l'équipe première est en haut du classement et les attaquants marquent des buts. De mon côté, je fais simplement mon travail. L'occasion finira par arriver et ce sera alors mon heure de me montrer.

In a recent development, comment je décrirais le niveau de la cinquième division française, notamment par rapport à la Première Ligue estonienne ? Je dirais clairement que le niveau est supérieur. Ce n'est pas non plus un immense fossé, mais le jeu est très physique. En face, on retrouve de grands gaillards, et pas des équipes réserves comme la nôtre. Bon, il y a encore un autre club réserve dans le championnat, mais toutes les autres équipes sont composées de joueurs professionnels. Le jeu est très physique et rapide.

According to recent reports, les séances de l'équipe première sont très intenses et difficiles pour tout le monde. Après l'entraînement, tout le monde termine les mains sur les genoux ! Les premières semaines après mon retour ont été difficiles, mais depuis, les choses vont de mieux en mieux. Je sens que je m'en sors finalement plutôt bien. Les entraîneurs me font également de bons retours et tout me convient.

Je ne saurais pas dire exactement à quel niveau je me situe par rapport aux autres joueurs de l'effectif pro, mais les entraîneurs insistent certainement auprès de nos jeunes joueurs sur la nécessité d'en faire davantage pour progresser et être prêts à être lancés dans le grand bain. Dans l'ensemble, ça se passe bien. Les entraîneurs veulent que je prenne davantage d'initiatives, que je demande plus souvent le ballon et que je sois encore plus actif. C'est ainsi que je pourrai continuer à progresser.

J'ai également joué au poste de numéro 10. Si je souhaite qu'on fasse de moi un joueur davantage impliqué dans la construction du jeu ? Oui. Chez nous, aussi bien l'équipe première que la réserve évoluent avec deux attaquants. Dans les deux équipes, l'un des deux décroche légèrement. Avec la réserve, j'ai également un autre attaquant à mes côtés, qui joue plutôt comme un véritable avant-centre.

It has been revealed that de mon côté, je suis davantage un joueur technique et c'est pour cette raison qu'on souhaite me voir évoluer plus souvent au poste de numéro 10. Cela me convient également, car c'est bien d'avoir plusieurs possibilités. En ce moment, je joue surtout à ce poste, voire même en faux numéro 9. J'ai également expliqué aux entraîneurs que, comme j'ai pratiquement toujours joué en tant qu'avant-centre, je préfère clairement évoluer à ce poste pour le moment. C'est celui auquel je suis le plus habitué.

Recent findings suggest that jouer numéro 10 avec la réserve reste encore un peu difficile. Il faut s'habituer à évoluer dans un système à deux attaquants. J'aime aussi davantage avoir le ballon et participer au jeu. Aujourd'hui, je dirais que c'est du 50-50 concernant mes préférences, mais pour le moment, j'aimerais quand même jouer davantage tout en haut de l'attaque.

Si je me suis habitué à la vie en France, à la langue française et à tout le reste ? Le français… Je n'ai pas vraiment envie de parler avec les gens, c'est difficile ! (Rires.) Je comprends la langue et nous suivons également des cours de français chaque semaine avec les autres joueurs étrangers. Mais lorsque je me promène en ville, je ne me sens pas encore complètement chez moi. L'environnement est tout de même assez différent, avec davantage de vie urbaine.

Recent findings suggest that si les rues de Saint-Etienne sont calmes ? Pas du tout ! Il y a des troubles dans toute la France et nous en avons également chez nous. Il y a eu des jours où dans toute la ville, les magasins étaient fermés et barricadés. Il y avait pas mal d'agitation. Cela ne perturbe pas du tout mes déplacements pour aller à l'entraînement. J'habite assez près et le centre d'entraînement se trouve également dans la partie haute de la ville, où il n'y a pas de gros problèmes.

Industry observers note that J'ai maintenant trouvé un appartement. Le club dispose d'un responsable qui s'occupe des joueurs et de leurs questions liées à la vie quotidienne. Grâce à lui, nous avons trouvé un appartement agréable à proximité. Personnellement, j'aurais préféré habiter un peu plus loin, mais comme je n'ai pas de voiture, cela aurait été un peu compliqué.

According to recent reports, si je sais me débrouiller tout seul, préparer des pâtes et faire ta lessive ? Bien sûr que je sais faire ! Ma mère s'inquiète beaucoup, mais moi, je m'en sors très bien ! (Rires.) Il n'y a pas vraiment de raison de s'inquiéter. Pour les repas, c'est assez simple : le club dispose d'un service de restauration qui prépare le dîner pour tous les joueurs qui le souhaitent. On peut ensuite récupérer son repas et l'emporter chez soi.

Mon temps libre, je joue un peu à la PlayStation, mais je sors également avec des amis, notamment les plus jeunes joueurs de l'équipe. Ils parlent français et pas vraiment anglais, donc ce n'est pas toujours évident. Mais ils sont vraiment sympas : ils essaient de baragouiner quelques mots en anglais et, de mon côté, je leur réponds en français. C'est un peu un mélange des deux langues, mais ça fonctionne très bien !

Industry observers note that pour être honnête, cette année a été très difficile pour moi mentalement. Quand je suis arrivé là-bas en février, je voulais évidemment commencer à jouer immédiatement. Mais ensuite, ce problème physique est apparu et la situation s'est prolongée, encore et encore. Heureusement, le club dispose d'un psychologue avec qui il est très facile de discuter. Je lui confie régulièrement tout ce que j'ai sur le cœur et il m'a énormément aidé. Ma famille, mes amis et mon agent m'ont également beaucoup soutenu.

According to recent reports, maintenant, ça va mieux. Je joue et je n'ai plus de problème. Il faut simplement continuer à avancer. Je n'ai pas vraiment souffert du mal du pays pendant cette période car j'ai toujours voulu vivre à l'étranger et mener une carrière de footballeur à l'étranger. Pour moi, cela a été assez facile, mais vous pouvez imaginer ce que ma famille a pu ressentir… Ma mère pleurait régulièrement au téléphone, alors que de mon côté, je le vivais plutôt bien. Je ne me faisais pas de souci à ce sujet. Je voulais simplement guérir et recommencer à jouer.

L'année dernière, lorsque j'étais en sélection en novembre, j'ai commencé à ressentir quelque chose vers la fin du rassemblement, avant le match contre Chypre. Mais ensuite, la douleur a disparu. Tout semblait simple, je n'avais aucun problème et je m'entraînais normalement. Mais il est possible que le rythme ait été particulièrement intense avec l'équipe première. Là-bas non plus, je n'avais pas vraiment de repos : j'ai immédiatement repris le travail et le même problème est revenu. La différence de charge de travail a donc pu jouer un rôle.

According to recent reports, si cela pourrait être lié à la croissance ? Certainement. Il faut aussi prendre en compte le fait que l'année dernière, lorsque je jouais au Vaprus, j'étais également présent à chaque rassemblement international avec les différentes sélections. Je ne prenais donc pas de repos, contrairement aux autres joueurs qui avaient tout de même quelques jours de congé. À chaque retour de sélection, je reprenais immédiatement l'entraînement et les matchs s'enchaînaient.

Ma taille ? 1,85 m. Cela fait déjà quelque temps. Dans quelle mesure le changement d'entraîneur l'été dernier à Saint-Etienne cela a modifié ou influencé ma situation ? Cela n'a rien changé. Lorsqu'il est arrivé, nous avons immédiatement discuté et il m'a dit qu'il m'appréciait et qu'il me voyait dans ses looks. Il fallait simplement que je retrouve la pleine forme et que je puisse désormais lui montrer progressivement ce dont je suis capable.".

Industry observers note that L'ancien Vert, Maedine Makhloufi, transféré à l'US Dunkerque le 13 janvier dernier foulera peut-être la pelouse de Geoffroy-Guichard le samedi 28 novembre prochain avec le FC Villefranche Beaujolais, pour le 8ème tour de la Coupe de France. En effet, le club caladois annonce le prêt du latéral gauche par le club nordiste : "Nous sommes heureux d’annoncer l’arrivée de Maedine Makhloufi, prêté par l’USL Dunkerque jusqu’à la fin de la saison !Formé à l’AS Saint Etienne de ses 8 ans jusqu’au monde senior, il signe en Ligue 2, à Dunkerque, l’an dernier."Maedine Makhloufi espère faire partie du onze qui viendra défier les Verts en Coupe de France : "Je suis très heureux d’être prêté au FCVB et de retrouver une région que je connais et que j’apprécie ! Le hasard du tirage va me faire retrouver l’ASSE et le chaudron. J’espère que ce sera un beau match et que le meilleur gagne".

Il va retrouver à Villefranche un autre ancien Vert, le défenseur central Marvin Tshibuabua.

Sources indicate that maedine Makhloufi était en manque de temps de jeu avec l'US Dunkerque :  sur les 12 rencontres disputées en Ligue 2, il n'a pas été retenu dans le groupe à 8 reprises, est resté sur le banc sans entrer à 3 reprises et n'est entré que pour 9 petites minutes contre Rodez le 30 octobre. La saison dernière, sur 16 matchs disputés par Dunkerque, il avait été titulaire à 3 reprises, était entré en jeu à 5 reprises. Lors de son entrée pour 4 minutes face à Boulogne, il avait inscrit 1 but lors de ce derby qui avait vu Dinkerque l'emporetr par 6 à 2.Avec les Verts, Maedine Makhloufi n'a disputé qu'un seul match en pro, contre la modeste équipe de Quetigny à Dijon en Coupe de France.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Feyenoord preserved their four-point advantage over champions PSV after coming away with a point from Eindhoven thanks to an improved second-half performance.

PSV dominated the first half as they deployed a close-passing, tiki-taka style to stifle Feyenoord, but only had Guus Til’s well-taken volley after 20 minutes to show for it.

Ten minutes after the break Feyenoord equalised when Anis Hadj Moussa was given too much space to charge down the right flank and bend a shot inside the far post.

The Algerian had a good chance for a second towards the end, while PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar had to be alert to keep out a header by Nacho Ferri from close range.

“We were by far the better team today and had the better chances,” mentioned PSV coach Peter Bosz. “We started the second half badly and made a mistake, after which Hadj Moussa scored. And even then we could have won it.”.

Ajax overtook PSV to close the gap at the top to three points with a hard-fought win at Sparta. Veteran striker Jens Toornstra scored for Sparta on his 500th Eredivisie appearance, but Abdellah Ouazane and Tolu Arokodare, the scorers against Atalanta in midweek, were on target again to claim the win for Ajax.

Twente moved up to fourth place as two late goals by Sondre Ørjasæter and Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink earned a 2-0 win at AZ Alkmaar, who like Twente and PSV have 20 points.

Fortuna Sittard also snatched the points late on against Excelsior as Rodrigo Guth headed in a corner in injury time to keep the Limburg club in sixth place, two points further back.

At the other end of the table, the return of Adrie Koster as veteran coach brought no relief to Willem II, who crashed to a 6-1 home defeat to Cambuur.

The Tilburgers remain four points behind ADO Den Haag, who were unable to keep up the momentum of last week’s win against PSV as they lost 3-2 at home to Heerenveen.

Telstar lost by the same margin at Go Ahead Eagles, whose striker Søren Tengstedt netted twice in the first half to lead the Eredivisie scoring charts with eight goals.

Willem II Tilburg 1-6 Cambuur Leeuwarden.

Sports club members becoming less tolerant of homosexuality

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents stated they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute said the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF remarked the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, mentioned it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La risonanza ha evidenziato un affaticamento, senza lesioni. Rovella e Gudmundsson hanno lavorato con il gruppo.

Davide Frattesi è tornato ad allenarsi regolarmente con il gruppo della Lazio dopo il problema ai flessori che lo aveva costretto a lasciare in anticipo il ritiro della Nazionale. Gli esami hanno escluso lesioni muscolari e, salvo imprevisti nelle prossime sedute, il centrocampista sarà a disposizione di Gennaro Gattuso per la gara contro il Lecce.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that il classe ’99, ex Inter, aveva lasciato Coverciano nei giorni scorsi per un fastidio accusato durante gli impegni con l’Italia. Aveva così saltato la sfida di Bruxelles contro il Belgio, mentre alla Lazio cresceva la preoccupazione per le sue condizioni.

Recent findings suggest that gli accertamenti strumentali e la risonanza magnetica effettuati nelle ultime ore hanno evidenziato un affaticamento, senza lesioni muscolari. Nella seduta odierna Frattesi ha lavorato con i compagni, mettendosi a disposizione dello staff tecnico dopo il rientro anticipato dal ritiro azzurro.

Industry observers note that se non arriveranno ricadute o altri imprevisti durante la preparazione, il centrocampista sarà convocabile per l’anticipo della 12ª giornata di Serie A contro il Lecce. La partita è in programma sabato 21 novembre alle 15:00 allo Stadio Olimpico.

It has been revealed that il recupero di Frattesi conta per la Lazio anche alla luce del suo rendimento recente. La mezzala è andata a segno nell’ultimo turno di campionato sul campo del Napoli. I suoi inserimenti e la sua freschezza atletica sono risorse per affrontare la difesa del Lecce alla ripresa del torneo.

In a recent development, la seduta ha dato a Gattuso altre indicazioni in vista della sfida con i salentini. Nicolò Rovella, Danilo Cataldi, Albert Gudmundsson, Tijjani Noslin e Kenneth Taylor hanno lavorato regolarmente in gruppo. Il loro coinvolgimento offre al tecnico più soluzioni a centrocampo e nel reparto offensivo.

In particolare, la presenza di Rovella e Gudmundsson amplia le possibilità di rotazione dell’allenatore in vista dei prossimi impegni ravvicinati. Anche per loro, dunque, l’allenamento con i compagni è un passaggio nella preparazione della gara contro il Lecce.

#3595. Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

📅 23 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 32m • 📚 Deep Dive (6419 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6419 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.
  • Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.
  • Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

Sources indicate that really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

It has been revealed that they were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

Sources indicate that dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

According to recent reports, “I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle said quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”.

Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

Sources indicate that one of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address quickly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

Off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

Sources indicate that an electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F.

As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

Industry observers note that “We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”.

It has been revealed that what could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

Recent findings suggest that this, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

Industry observers note that cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK.

Industry observers note that “We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola said. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

“You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”.

There will be a powerful expression of unity between Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters in memory of their shared icon, Kevin Keegan, before this afternoon’s game.

A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

The cooperation between the two to ensure St James’ Park can deliver a special tribute to a remarkable figure in English football has been heartwarming.

The sale of Curtis Jones to Inter Milan means that for the first time since Liverpool came into existence in 1892, the prospect of them going through the season without fielding a player who was born in the city for a game is real. He has also not sugar-coated anything. Jaissle knows he is up against it. Time is the enemy, given how late he arrived in pre-season and he understands the size of the task ahead.

According to recent reports, these are early days, but the energy and purpose he has brought to the job have impressed everyone at all levels of the club. Clear communication is at the heart of everything. He explains what he expects, what he needs and what has to be done, no matter who the conversation is with.

It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

Recent findings suggest that this fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.Full team news on the way shortly.

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he mentioned. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”.

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop mentioned the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 4-0 Go Ahead Eagles.

Tech Report: Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dutchnews

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND remarked the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

The Dutch football association KNVB introduced an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser said it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

Industry observers note that “Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players noted they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius stated he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

Industry observers note that “I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that says I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

In a recent development, this was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the latest Chelsea manager.

According to recent reports, that was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

Sources indicate that alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he mentioned, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE.

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN.

Industry observers note that chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a significant decision is looming for Alonso.

Sources indicate that in terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB.

According to recent reports, it was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v.

Recent findings suggest that "Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq.

In a recent development, “I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”.

Recent findings suggest that palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”.

It has been revealed that if there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

In a recent development, arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will rapidly become familiar.

Industry observers note that there was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

Industry observers note that “We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we indicated character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

Recent findings suggest that “We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”.

No more excuses. No more jam tomorrow. It is time for Chelsea to fight for the Premier League title this season. Anything else should be deemed a disappointment.

This is Chelsea version 3.0 under BlueCo, who bought the club four years ago. First there was Todd Boehly’s trolley dash, then came Behdad Eghbali’s youth club. This summer the focus has been on being Premier League-ready.

Two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the new Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

“I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa remarked. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”.

Arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

Chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

Recent findings suggest that “We feel ready,” Alonso stated. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”.

Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

Recent findings suggest that “Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”.

These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

Gli agenti hanno sondato i major: il Brentford ha chiesto Isaksen e la Juventus è pronta a offrire 40 milioni per Taylor.

Per la Lazio resta aperta la possibilità di operare nel mercato di gennaio a saldo zero, anziché subire un nuovo blocco totale. Lotito lavora da due mesi per trovare una soluzione. La decisione arriverà a dicembre dalla Commissione di controllo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that A settembre il blocco invernale sembrava inevitabile, dopo gli acquisti estivi e la crescita del monte ingaggi. Ora nei conti biancocelesti si intravede uno spiraglio, seppure stretto. Lotito procede senza annunci, tra trattative, incastri e verifiche dei conti; a Formello restano prudenza e speranza.

It has been revealed that la Commissione di controllo, che ieri ha firmato un protocollo d’intesa con la Consob, darà la risposta definitiva a dicembre. Fino a quel momento, l’ipotesi del saldo zero rimane aperta, ma non è una certezza.

Industry observers note that nel frattempo è pronto un piano alternativo. Gli agenti hanno sondato il mercato, raccolto offerte e valutato i substantial della Lazio. La linea del club, però, è quella promessa a Gattuso: nessuna cessione a gennaio.

Il Brentford ha chiesto Isaksen. Anche la Juventus potrebbe scontrarsi con la stessa posizione: è pronta a mettere sul tavolo 40 milioni per Taylor. La linea sulle cessioni è riassunta così: «In uscita non si muove nessuno». Almeno per ora, in attesa della decisione prevista prima di Natale.

In a upcoming feature PortuGOAL will be bringing you some recommended reading about Portuguese football from around the web, penned by our own network of writers or others.

We kick off by alerting you to a superb interview in the Guardian by Nick Ames with Port Vale's Portuguese manager Bruno Ribeiro. The headline writer focused on Ribeiro's relationship with José Mourinho, but it is the detail of Ribeiro's struggle to make things work at an English third-tier team of meagre resources that makes for fascinating insight.

Benfica are top of the Liga NOS and their coach Rui Vitória continues to confound the doubters who believed he would not be up to the job at the Lisbon giants. Simon Curtis takes a look at "the quiet man at the helm of a national institution". And Benfica fans, while we've got your attention, a shout out for Tom Kundert's profile of the club's world-renowned Seixal Academy for ESPN.

Talking about Portuguese football schools, none has produced more top-class players in recent decades than Sporting's Alcochete Academy, and the excellent Outside of the Boot website has a brilliantly detailed profile written by Mateus Carvalho of another possible gem for the Lions, Francisco Geraldes, who is currently on loan at Moreirense.

Industry observers note that to finish up this initial trip around the net, we alert you to FourFourTwo's list of the 59 best Under-21 footballers from around the world. The section we highlight has a mini profile of Porto striker André Silva, who will be hoping to net his first senior international goal tonight for the Seleção against Andorra. In case you're wondering, the British magazine rank him at number 23.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona sporting director Deco has left the door wide open for Liverpool to sign Ronald Araujo permanently.

The Uruguayan joined the Reds on a season-long loan in August and has made an immediate impression on the Anfield faithful, putting in a series of tremendous performances at right-back for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Reports from Spain in recent days have indicated that Merseyside chiefs are keen to take up the option to sign the defender outright for £47m, with the player also understood to be ready to stay in L4 beyond next summer.

Liverpool’s chances of securing him on a permanent basis would appear to have been greatly boosted by comments from Deco.

Industry observers note that the Barcelona chief told Catalunya Radio’s Tot Costa: “A bit of money wouldn’t hurt us either. We’d be happy because things have gone well, and we’d be happy for him too.

Sources indicate that “Personally, I’m happy for Ronald. He’s one of the team’s leaders. He’s been through some difficult times and some happy ones at the club, and we have a good relationship.

“He’s made his decision, and we respect it. The most notable thing for us is to see him happy. If he decides to stay and things carry on like this, we’d be happy with that too.”.

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

It seems that, if Liverpool were to sign Araujo permanently, everyone would be a winner.

The Reds would secure a player who’s been excellent for them (and get a deal done at a relatively modest fee), the defender would get to remain on Merseyside (where his family are reportedly very happy), and Barcelona would bank nearly £50m for someone they’re seemingly happy to let go.

Even with Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni finally back in first-team training, both of them will realistically need a few more weeks to be properly matchday ready, so Iraola will continue to depend heavily on the Uruguayan to maintain form and fitness.

Liverpool won’t be able to activate the purchase option on Araujo until the end of the season, and it’s not implausible that he could succumb to a serious injury or see his performance levels drop in the meantime.

According to recent reports, right now, though, there’s no excuse for Anfield chiefs not to go all-out to secure a permanent transfer, especially with Deco indicating that Barcelona would be prepared to sanction his sale. Don’t fumble this one please, Julian Ward!

Suivant de près l'actualité du MHSC, Benjamin Psaume est revenu dans le podcast Montpellier Sport Club (relayé par Allez Paillade) sur le match de Coupe de France qui a vu les Héraultais écraser (5-0) le FC Balagne en Corse. L'ancien joueur de Toulouse, Nîmes, Arles-Avignon, Troyes et Le Puy ne tarit pas d'éloges sur Zoumana Camara :.

"En coupe de France, dans des matchs comme cela où il manque beaucoup de monde, le plus crucial c’est la qualification. Zoumana Camara a lancé des jeunes. C’est à l’image de ce qu’il montre depuis le début de saison. Il a tellement fédéré le groupe et le vestiaire que peu importe les joueurs qu’il peut mettre, on sent qu’ils sont animés par une envie. Ils ne réfléchissent pas au contexte même s’il est particulier, ils ont envie de faire mal à l’adversaire. Ils ont un enthousiasme dès la première minute. Ils répondent présents. Et quand tu marques à la première minute dans des matchs comme ça, je me suis dit que c’était terminé même si après ils ont eu des occasions. Quand tu es le gros face au “petit”, tu sais que si tu ouvres le score c’est plus facile.

Le football a changé car avant, ils mettaient le bus et là tu arrives à les prendre dans la profondeur au bout d’une minute. Cela n’existait pas à mon époque quand tu allais jouer chez une équipe de niveau inférieur. Il n’y a pas eu trop de coups, le synthétique n’a pas joué de mauvais tour non plus. Il n’y a pas eu l’ambiance corse qu’il y avait avant. Tu te rends le match facile. On a découvert des jeunes joueurs. Ils ont réussi sur un tour où on ne leur en aurait pas voulu sur la manière à la mettre pour l’emporter en respectant l’adversaire. Ils ont donné une bonne image du club, ils ont également laissé la recette. À deux ou trois à zéro, ils ont continué. Ce vestiaire, ce groupe là, dans la psychologie, cela m’aurait étonné qu’ils prennent le match de haut. C’est très intéressant et à l’image de ce que l’on voit depuis le début de la saison.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

Sources indicate that referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst stated wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst mentioned. “What do you do about that?”.

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente said the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

Industry observers note that “This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”.

In a recent development, van Bronckhorst noted he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

According to recent reports, “Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”.

As part of PortuGOAL’s efforts to constantly evolve and serve lovers of Portuguese football with top-quality and increasingly accessible content, we are replacing the PortuGOAL Android and Apple APPs with a new Progressive Web Application (PWA) as from tomorrow, Tuesday 3 April.

It has been revealed that this significant step forward in phone apps technology loads the content instantly, even in areas of low connectivity, stays up to date at all times, displays the most recent version upon launching, is more efficient than native apps, works on-demand and is always accessible, without taking up a smartphone’s valuable memory or data. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.
  • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.
  • The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his latest club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

Leeds manager Daniel Farke mentioned: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Recent findings suggest that forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He stated: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

In a recent development, “For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

Recent findings suggest that “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

In a recent development, the most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

Recent findings suggest that of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

A tough night for the home teams...
